skill.name: data-substrate-analysis

content.value_statement: Data models and state updates can drift without clear review. This skill guides analysis of typing, mutation, and serialization choices.
actual_capabilities: Identify common type modeling approaches such as Pydantic, dataclasses, TypedDict, NamedTuple, and plain dictionaries.
Compare mutable and immutable state update patterns in selected code paths.
Review serialization choices including Pydantic dumps, dataclass conversion, custom methods, pickle, and JSON.
Produce a structured Markdown report covering typing strategy, core primitives, mutation risk, and serialization.
Connect findings to related architecture analysis workflows named in the skill.
limitations: It provides analysis guidance only and does not execute scanners or modify code.
Results depend on the caller providing relevant source files and repository context.
It does not prove concurrency safety without tests or runtime evidence.
It may need companion mapping skills to locate type and state files.

use_cases.title: Assess State Models
use_cases.description: Review how service state is represented, mutated, and serialized before a refactor.

use_cases.title: Review Framework Migration
use_cases.description: Compare Pydantic, dataclass, and TypedDict patterns during a framework or version migration.

use_cases.title: Document Data Contracts
use_cases.description: Create a concise map of core data primitives, validation boundaries, and lifecycle risks.

prompt_templates.title: Find Data Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Use data-substrate-analysis on this repository. Identify the main type files and classify each data modeling approach.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Mutation Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the state update paths in these files. Separate in-place mutation from copy-based updates and identify concurrency risks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Serialization Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review serialization and deserialization paths. Explain validation coverage, unknown field handling, and risks around nested objects.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Architecture Decision Input
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a data substrate report for this codebase. Compare modeling options and recommend changes for safer state lifecycle management.

output_examples.input: Review a Python API that uses Pydantic models and mutable service state.
output_examples.output: The report identifies Pydantic as primary, flags mutable state updates in service layers, and recommends copy-based updates for shared state.

output_examples.input: Compare a dataclass-based CLI with a TypedDict-based worker.
output_examples.output: The comparison highlights validation gaps, serialization trade-offs, and where explicit boundary checks would reduce data shape drift.

best_practices: Provide the files that define models, state containers, serializers, and API boundaries.
Ask for line-level evidence when using the result for architecture or refactoring decisions.
Pair this analysis with tests when changing mutation or serialization behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the report as a complete security audit.
Do not infer runtime safety from type annotations alone.
Do not skip context about framework versions or migration goals.

faq.question: Does this skill change my code?
faq.answer: No. It guides analysis and documentation of data modeling patterns.

faq.question: Can it compare Pydantic and TypedDict?
faq.answer: Yes. It classifies both approaches and describes validation, nesting, and serialization trade-offs.

faq.question: Does it require a specific language?
faq.answer: It is written for Python-oriented patterns, but the questions can guide other ecosystems.

faq.question: Can it find every state object automatically?
faq.answer: No. It works best when paired with repository mapping or targeted file lists.

faq.question: Is pickle usage automatically unsafe?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks reviewers to examine trust boundaries and deserialization context.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
